guides.title: Set the school up, in the right order
guides.summary: Everything else depends on this chain. Doing it out of order is the usual cause of an empty class list or a fee that will not attach.
steps: Manage ▸ Academic Year — create the running year first. Nothing can be created without a year to sit in.
Manage ▸ Sections — add the sections a class is split into (A, B, Science…).
Manage ▸ Courses/Subjects — add every subject the school teaches.
Manage ▸ Classes/Periods — create each class for this year, then attach its subjects and teachers.
Manage ▸ Fees — create the fee heads and their amounts for each class.
Enrollment ▸ Student — only now enroll students, so each one lands in a class that already has fees and subjects.
tips: A class belongs to one academic year. When the year changes you create the classes again for the new year — you do not rename last year's.

guides.title: Give a staff member their own login
guides.summary: Each person should sign in as themselves — shared logins make the history reports useless.
steps: Enroll the person under Enrollment ▸ Staff first, so there is a staff record to attach the login to.
Open Manage ▸ Users and create an account for them.
Open their staff profile ▸ Permissions and tick only the pages that person actually needs.
Hand over the username and password; ask them to change it from Profile after signing in.
tips: Permissions are per page. Someone who only collects fees needs Payment, not Accounting.

guides.title: Put your logo and signatures on printed documents
guides.summary: Bills, marksheets and certificates print whatever is uploaded here.
steps: Open Profile.
In 'Logos and signatures', click the image you want to replace.
Pick a clear image with a white or transparent background and confirm the upload.
Print any bill to check it before a whole batch is printed.
tips: The school's name, PAN and dates are held by CentIT — contact support to have those corrected.

guides.title: Enroll a new student
guides.summary: One student, with guardian details, class and fees attached in a single pass.
steps: Open Enrollment ▸ Student.
Fill the personal details, then the guardian's name and contact — the guardian contact is the number every SMS goes to.
Pick the academic year, class and section.
Attach the fees that apply to this student, and any discount.
Save. The student now appears in that class everywhere in the system.
tips: If the guardian contact is wrong or missing, that student silently receives no SMS at all.
Enrolling many students at once? Use Enrollment ▸ Bulk ▸ Student enrollments instead.

guides.title: Move a student to another class or section
guides.summary: Changing a class carries the student's outstanding dues with them; changing a section can carry their results.
steps: Search the student and open their profile.
Change the class or section and save.
Check the student's ledger afterwards to confirm the balance came across as expected.
tips: A section change moves the student's recorded results with them automatically — you do not need to re-enter marks.
Old dues are carried forward on a class change. If a balance looks wrong after a move, tell support the student's name before doing anything else.

guides.title: Collect a fee and print the receipt
guides.summary: The everyday counter job.
steps: Open Payment ▸ Student and search the student.
Check the outstanding rows and the balance shown.
Enter the amount received against the correct fee titles.
Choose the payment month, then save — wait for the button to finish before clicking again.
Print the receipt for the guardian.
tips: Never double-click Save on a slow connection: the button disables itself while it is working, and a second click is how duplicate receipts get created.
Put the money against the fee titles it was actually paid for. Dumping a lump into 'Old Dues' makes every later report harder to read.

guides.title: Post monthly fees to a whole class
guides.summary: Charges the month's fees to every student in a class in one action.
steps: Open Payment ▸ Ledger posting.
Pick the academic year, class and section.
Pick the month you are charging for — this is required, and it is what every monthly report groups by.
Select the fee titles to post and check the amounts.
Post, then spot-check one student's ledger to confirm it landed.
tips: Posting the same month twice charges twice. Check Reports ▸ Recent postings before re-posting.

guides.title: Enter dues carried over from before the system
guides.summary: Opening balances for students who already owed money when you started.
steps: Open Payment ▸ Old dues posting.
Pick the class, then enter each student's carried-over amount.
Save, and verify the total against your previous register.
tips: Old dues are exempt from the month requirement — they belong to no single month by definition.

guides.title: Send home a dues reminder bill
guides.summary: A printed bill per student showing what is still owed.
steps: Open Payment ▸ Reminder bills.
Pick the class and section.
Review the list, then print — several bills lay out per sheet.
tips: Prefer a text message? SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send Dues Reminder does the same thing by SMS.

guides.title: Find out who still owes money
guides.summary: The report to open before a fee drive.
steps: Open Reports ▸ Overall Remaining dues.
Filter to the class or the whole school.
Use the Columns button to hide anything you do not need before printing or exporting.
tips: Every report honours the columns you have left visible when it prints or exports.

guides.title: Set up an exam
guides.summary: Do this before anyone tries to enter marks.
steps: Exam and result ▸ Exam — create the exam (First Terminal, Final…) for this academic year.
Exam and result ▸ Schedule — set the date and time per subject.
Exam and result ▸ Grading rules — confirm the pass marks and grade bands.
Exam and result ▸ Entry cards — print admit cards for the students.
tips: If a subject is missing from marks entry, it is not attached to that class under Manage ▸ Classes/Periods.

guides.title: Enter marks and publish results
guides.summary: From an empty mark sheet to a printable marksheet.
steps: Print Exam and result ▸ Marks entry slip and give it to each subject teacher.
Open Exam and result ▸ Marks entry, pick the exam, class, section and subject.
Type the marks and save — the page saves per subject, so finish one before moving on.
Enter extra activities under Exam and result ▸ Extra activities entry, if the school uses them.
Exam and result ▸ Publish results, then print from Exam and result ▸ Results.
tips: A subject that was taught but has no marks column shows as blank on the marksheet — check the class's subject list rather than re-entering.

guides.title: Take attendance for the day
guides.summary: Manually, from the class register.
steps: Open App ▸ Attendance ▸ Student Attendance entry.
Pick the class, section and date.
Mark the absent students; everyone else is counted present.
Save. Guardians of present and absent students receive an app notification.
tips: The absent-student SMS is not sent automatically. Send it deliberately from SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send Messages.

guides.title: When the RFID device shows no new attendance
guides.summary: Almost always the device, not the system.
steps: Open App ▸ RFID ▸ Attendance Logs and look at the date of the last log.
If it stopped on a particular day, check the device's power and internet at the school.
Once it is back online, use the Pull logs button to fetch everything it recorded while it was offline.
tips: Any punch counts as present, and the earliest punch of the day is taken as the check-in time.
A card only works after the person is registered under App ▸ RFID ▸ Users Setup.

guides.title: Turn SMS on for the school
guides.summary: One API key, entered once. Nothing sends until it is there.
guides.where: SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ SMS Settings
steps: Open SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ SMS Settings.
Follow the Help steps on that page to create a token in the SMS portal.
Paste the Auth Token into 'SMS API Key' and save.
Write your message wording under SMS ▸ SMS Templates.
tips: Every send costs one credit per recipient. The credit balance is shown at the top of each SMS page.

guides.title: Send an SMS to a group of guardians
guides.summary: A holiday notice, a meeting call, a fee reminder.
guides.where: SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send Bulk SMS
steps: Open SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send Bulk SMS.
Filter to the students you mean — by class, by name, or by bus station.
Search, then check the count against your SMS credits.
Write the message. Use the place values to drop in each student's own name.
Send.
tips: Bulk SMS goes to the guardian's contact number, not the student's.

guides.title: Send an SMS to teachers and staff
guides.summary: Straight to the staff member's own phone, not a guardian's.
guides.where: SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send SMS to Staff
steps: Open SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ Send SMS to Staff.
Filter by name, role or employment status — leave it blank for every employed staff member.
Search and check the count against your SMS credits.
Write the message; the place values fill in each person's name and designation.
Send.
tips: It sends to the staff member's primary contact. Anyone without one is skipped and reported back to you.

guides.title: Wish students and teachers on their birthday
guides.summary: Sent automatically each morning, once per person, from your own template.
guides.where: SMS ▸ SMS Templates, then Profile ▸ settings
steps: Open SMS and Communication ▸ SMS ▸ SMS Templates.
Write the 'Birthday Wish SMS Template' for students and the 'Staff Birthday Wish SMS Template' for teachers and staff.
Open Profile ▸ SMS and Notification Settings and switch on the birthday wishes you want.
Save. From the next morning, anyone whose birth date falls on that day is wished automatically.
tips: A birth date has to be recorded for the wish to fire — staff birth dates live on the staff member's Other info tab.

guides.title: Pay salaries for the month
guides.summary: Post the month's salary, then record the payment.
steps: Payroll ▸ Salary posting — post the month's salary for the staff you are paying.
Payroll ▸ Payment — record what was actually paid to each person.
Payroll ▸ Pay slips — print the slips.
Payroll ▸ Salary sheet — the month's summary, including TDS, PF and insurance deductions.
tips: PF and insurance are fixed monthly deductions taken at payment time. Net pay = gross − TDS − PF − insurance.

guides.title: Record an income or an expense
guides.summary: Double-entry vouchers, with the reports built from them.
steps: Accounting ▸ Create Ledger — make sure the ledger head you need exists.
Accounting ▸ Income Entry or Expense Entry — enter the voucher and save.
Accounting ▸ Income Entries / Expense Entries — find, view or reprint it later.
Accounting ▸ Reports — Trial Balance, Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet.
tips: A deleted voucher still appears in the entry lists with a red 'Deleted' badge, for viewing and reprinting only. Reports exclude it.
You can open a closed fiscal year to read it — past years are viewable, not editable.

guides.title: Issue and return a book
guides.summary: Scan or search, issue, and take it back later.
steps: Library ▸ Library Setup — set the loan period and the fine per day, once.
Library ▸ Books — add the titles and their copies.
Library ▸ Book Issue/Return — find the member, find the book, issue it.
On return, open the same page; any fine is calculated for you.
tips: The accession number of a copy is its own number in the system — it is unique across every school sharing the library.
Issuing to a student from another school? Add them under 'Other schools' on the issue page.

guides.title: Promote students to the next class
guides.summary: The move from this academic year into the next one.
steps: Create the next academic year under Manage ▸ Academic Year.
Create next year's classes, subjects and fees before promoting anyone.
Open Enrollment ▸ Class Promotion, pick the class, and promote the students who passed.
Check a few students afterwards: correct new class, and their outstanding dues carried across.
tips: Promote only after next year's classes exist, otherwise there is nowhere for the students to land.
Students leaving the school should be marked as such rather than promoted.

guides.title: Close the academic year
guides.summary: Locks last year's records and rolls balances forward. Not reversible on your own.
steps: Finish every fee collection, marks entry and result publication for the year first.
Open Manage ▸ Academic year closing and read the impact summary it shows you.
Check the carried-forward dues on that summary before confirming.
Confirm the close.
tips: Closing is a large, hard-to-undo step. If anything on the impact summary looks wrong, stop and call support before confirming.
A closed year stays readable — results and reports for it can still be opened and printed.
